```python
from datetime import datetime
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from flask_login import UserMixin
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

db = SQLAlchemy()

class User(UserMixin, db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    role = db.Column(db.String(20), default='developer')  # developer, admin
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    def set_password(self, password):
        self.password_hash = generate_password_hash(password)

    def check_password(self, password):
        return check_password_hash(self.password_hash, password)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

class Project(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text)
    created_by = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    # Relationship with User
    creator = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('projects', lazy=True))

    # Relationship with Documents
    documents = db.relationship('Document', backref='project', lazy=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Project {self.name}>'

class Document(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    content = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    file_path = db.Column(db.String(255))  # For uploaded files
    document_type = db.Column(db.String(50))  # api, spec, design, etc.
    project_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('project.id'), nullable=False)
    created_by = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    # Version history
    versions = db.relationship('DocumentVersion', backref='document', lazy=True)
    version_count = db.Column(db.Integer, default=1)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Document {self.title}>'

class DocumentVersion(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    document_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('document.id'), nullable=False)
    content = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    version_number = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)
    created_by = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<DocumentVersion {self.version_number}>'

class ProjectPermission(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    project_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('project.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    permission_level = db.Column(db.String(20), default='read')  # read, write, admin
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<ProjectPermission {self.project_id} - {self.user_id}>'

class ApiEndpoint(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    document_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('document.id'), nullable=False)
    endpoint = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    method = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text)
    request_body = db.Column(db.Text)
    response_body = db.Column(db.Text)
    status_code = db.Column(db.String(50))
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<ApiEndpoint {self.endpoint}>'

class ChangeLog(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    document_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('document.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'), nullable=False)
    action = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)  # created, updated, deleted
    details = db.Column(db.Text)
    timestamp = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<ChangeLog {self.id}>'
```

```python
from flask import Flask, render_template, request, redirect, url_for, flash, jsonify, session
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash
from datetime import datetime
import os
import markdown
import json
from functools import wraps

# Initialize Flask app
app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = 'your-secret-key-here'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///documentation.db'
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

# Initialize extensions
db = SQLAlchemy(app)
login_manager = LoginManager(app)
login_manager.login_view = 'login'

# Custom decorator for admin only
def admin_required(f):
    @wraps(f)
    def decorated_function(*args, **kwargs):
        if not current_user.is_authenticated or current_user.role != 'admin':
            return redirect(url_for('login'))
        return f(*args, **kwargs)
    return decorated_function

# User loader
@login_manager.user_loader
def load_user(user_id):
    return User.query.get(int(user_id))

# Initialize database
def init_db():
    db.create_all()
    # Create default admin user
    if not User.query.filter_by(username='admin').first():
        admin_user = User(username='admin', email='admin@example.com', role='admin')
        admin_user.set_password('admin123')
        db.session.add(admin_user)
        db.session.commit()

# Forms
class LoginForm(FlaskForm):
    username = StringField('Username', validators=[DataRequired()])
    password = PasswordField('Password', validators=[DataRequired()])
    submit = SubmitField('Login')

class RegistrationForm(FlaskForm):
    username = StringField('Username', validators=[DataRequired(), Length(min=3, max=80)])
    email = StringField('Email', validators=[DataRequired(), Email()])
    password = PasswordField('Password', validators=[DataRequired(), Length(min=6)])
    submit = SubmitField('Register')

class DocumentForm(FlaskForm):
    title = StringField('Document Title', validators=[DataRequired()])
    content = TextAreaField('Document Content', validators=[DataRequired()])
    document_type = SelectField('Document Type', choices=[('api', 'API Documentation'), 
                                                          ('spec', 'Technical Specification'), 
                                                          ('design', 'System Design'), 
                                                          ('other', 'Other')])
    project_id = SelectField('Project', choices=[], coerce=int)
    submit = SubmitField('Save Document')

class ApiEndpointForm(FlaskForm):
    endpoint = StringField('Endpoint', validators=[DataRequired()])
    method = SelectField('HTTP Method', choices=[('GET', 'GET'), ('POST', 'POST'), 
                                                 ('PUT', 'PUT'), ('DELETE', 'DELETE')])
    description = TextAreaField('Description')
    request_body = TextAreaField('Request Body')
    response_body = TextAreaField('Response Body')
    status_code = StringField('Status Code')
    submit = SubmitField('Add Endpoint')

class ProjectPermissionForm(FlaskForm):
    user_id = SelectField('User', choices=[], coerce=int)
    project_id = SelectField('Project', choices=[], coerce=int)
    permission_level = SelectField('Permission Level', choices=[('read', 'Read'), 
                                                               ('write', 'Write'), 
                                                               ('admin', 'Admin')])
    submit = SubmitField('Assign Permission')

# Routes
@app.route('/')
def index():
    if current_user.is_authenticated:
        return redirect(url_for('dashboard'))
    return redirect(url_for('login'))

@app.route('/login', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def login():
    if current_user.is_authenticated:
        return redirect(url_for('dashboard'))
    
    form = LoginForm()
    if form.validate_on_submit():
        user = User.query.filter_by(username=form.username.data).first()
        if user and user.check_password(form.password.data):
            login_user(user)
            flash('Logged in successfully.', 'success')
            return redirect(url_for('dashboard'))
        else:
            flash('Invalid username or password.', 'error')
    
    return render_template('login.html', form=form)

@app.route('/logout')
@login_required
def logout():
    logout_user()
    flash('You have been logged out.', 'info')
    return redirect(url_for('login'))

@app.route('/register', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def register():
    if current_user.is_authenticated:
        return redirect(url_for('dashboard'))
    
    form = RegistrationForm()
    if form.validate_on_submit():
        user = User(username=form.username.data, email=form.email.data, role='developer')
        user.set_password(form.password.data)
        db.session.add(user)
        db.session.commit()
        flash('Account created successfully. Please log in.', 'success')
        return redirect(url_for('login'))
    
    return render_template('register.html', form=form)

@app.route('/dashboard')
@login_required
def dashboard():
    # Get user's projects
    projects = Project.query.filter(Project.creator_id == current_user.id).all()
    # Get all documents for user's projects
    documents = []
    for project in projects:
        project_docs = Document.query.filter_by(project_id=project.id).all()
        documents.extend(project_docs)
    
    # Get recent changes
    recent_changes = ChangeLog.query.order_by(ChangeLog.timestamp.desc()).limit(10).all()
    
    return render_template('dashboard.html', 
                          documents=documents, 
                          projects=projects, 
                          recent_changes=recent_changes)

@app.route('/documents')
@login_required
def documents():
    # Get all documents the user has access to
    documents = []
    for project in current_user.projects:
        project_docs = Document.query.filter_by(project_id=project.id).all()
        documents.extend(project_docs)
    
    return render_template('documents.html', documents=documents)

@app.route('/document/<int:document_id>')
@login_required
def view_document(document_id):
    document = Document.query.get_or_404(document_id)
    
    # Check if user has access to this document
    if not has_access_to_document(document):
        flash('You do not have permission to view this document.', 'error')

    # Get document versions

    return render_template('document.html',

@app.route('/api/endpoint', methods=['POST'])
@login_required
def add_api_endpoint():
    try:
        data = request.get_json()
        document_id = data.get('document_id')
        endpoint = data.get('endpoint')
        method = data.get('method')
        description = data.get('description')
        request_body = data.get('request_body')
        response_body = data.get('response_body')
        status_code = data.get('status_code')
        
        if not all([document_id, endpoint, method]):
            return jsonify({'error': 'Missing required fields'}), 400
        
        # Check if user has access to the document
        document = Document.query.get(document_id)
        if not has_access_to_document(document):
            return jsonify({'error': 'Permission denied'}), 403
        
        # Create new API endpoint
        api_endpoint = ApiEndpoint(
            document_id=document_id,
            endpoint=endpoint,
            method=method,
            description=description,
            request_body=request_body,
            response_body=response_body,
            status_code=status_code
        )
        db.session.add(api_endpoint)
        db.session.commit()
        
        # Create change log
        create_change_log(document_id, current_user.id, 'updated', 
                         f'Added API endpoint: {endpoint}')
        
        return jsonify({'success': True, 'message': 'API endpoint added successfully'})

        if request.method == 'PUT':
            data = request.get_json()
            endpoint.endpoint = data.get('endpoint', endpoint.endpoint)
            endpoint.method = data.get('method', endpoint.method)
            endpoint.description = data.get('description', endpoint.description)
            endpoint.request_body = data.get('request_body', endpoint.request_body)
            endpoint.response_body = data.get('response_body', endpoint.response_body)
            endpoint.status_code = data.get('status_code', endpoint.status_code)
            endpoint.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()
            db.session.commit()
            
            create_change_log(endpoint.document_id, current_user.id, 'updated', 
                             f'Updated API endpoint: {endpoint.endpoint}')
            
            return jsonify({'success': True, 'message': 'API endpoint updated successfully'})
        
        elif request.method == 'DELETE':
            db.session.delete(endpoint)
            db.session.commit()
            
            create_change_log(endpoint.document_id, current_user.id, 'deleted', 
                             f'Deleted API endpoint: {endpoint.endpoint}')
            
            return jsonify({'success': True, 'message': 'API endpoint deleted successfully'})
        
    except Exception as e:

@app.route('/api/v1/documents')
@login_required
def api_documents():
    # Get documents based on user's permissions
    documents = []
    for project in current_user.projects:
        project_docs = Document.query.filter_by(project_id=project.id).all()
        documents.extend(project_docs)
    
    # Convert to JSON format
    result = []
    for doc in documents:
        result.append({
            'id': doc.id,
            'title': doc.title,
            'document_type': doc.document_type,
            'created_at': doc.created_at.isoformat(),
            'updated_at': doc.updated_at.isoformat(),
            'project_name': project.name if project else 'Unknown'
        })
    
    return jsonify(result)

@app.route('/api/v1/documents/<int:document_id>')
@login_required
def api_document(document_id):
    document = Document.query.get_or_404(document_id)
    
    # Check if user has access
    if not has_access_to_document(document):
        return jsonify({'error': 'Permission denied'}), 403
    
    # Get API endpoints for this document
    api_endpoints = ApiEndpoint.query.filter_by(document_id=document_id).all()
    endpoints = []
    for endpoint in api_endpoints:
        endpoints.append({
            'id': endpoint.id,
            'endpoint': endpoint.endpoint,
            'method': endpoint.method,
            'description': endpoint.description,
            'request_body': endpoint.request_body,
            'response_body': endpoint.response_body,
            'status_code': endpoint.status_code
        })
    
    return jsonify({
        'document': {
            'id': document.id,
            'title': document.title,
            'content': document.content,
            'document_type': document.document_type,
            'created_at': document.created_at.isoformat(),
            'updated_at': document.updated_at.isoformat()
        },
        'api_endpoints': endpoints
    })

@app.route('/api/v1/versions/<int:document_id>')
@login_required
def api_versions(document_id):
    document = Document.query.get_or_404(document_id)
    
    # Check if user has access
    if not has_access_to_document(document):
        return jsonify({'error': 'Permission denied'}), 403
    
    versions = DocumentVersion.query.filter_by(document_id=document_id).order_by(DocumentVersion.version_number.desc()).all()
    
    result = []
    for version in versions:
        result.append({
            'version': version.version_number,
            'content': version.content,
            'created_at': version.created_at.isoformat(),
            'created_by': User.query.get(version.created_by).username if version.created_by else 'Unknown'
        })
    
    return jsonify(result)

# Helper functions
def has_access_to_document(document, permission_level='read'):
    """Check if current user has access to the document"""
    # Check if user is admin
    if current_user.role == 'admin':
        return True
    
    # Check if user is creator of the document
    if current_user.id == document.created_by:
        return True
    
    # Check if user has project access
    project = Project.query.get(document.project_id)
    if not project:
        return False
    
    # Check project permissions
    permission = ProjectPermission.query.filter_by(
        project_id=project.id, 
        user_id=current_user.id
    ).first()
    
    if permission and permission.permission_level in ['read', 'write', 'admin']:
        return True
    
    return False

def create_document_version(document_id, content):
    """Create a new version of the document"""
    document = Document.query.get(document_id)
    if not document:
        return
    
    # Get current version count
    current_version = DocumentVersion.query.filter_by(document_id=document_id).order_by(DocumentVersion.version_number.desc()).first()
    version_number = 1 if not current_version else current_version.version_number + 1
    
    # Create new version
    version = DocumentVersion(
        document_id=document_id,
        content=content,
        version_number=version_number,
        created_by=current_user.id
    )
    db.session.add(version)
    db.session.commit()
    
    # Update document version count
    document.version_count = version_number
    db.session.commit()

def create_change_log(document_id, user_id, action, details):
    """Create a change log entry"""
    change_log = ChangeLog(
        document_id=document_id,
        user_id=user_id,
        action=action,
        details=details
    )
    db.session.add(change_log)
    db.session.commit()

# Error handlers
@app.errorhandler(404)
def not_found_error(error):
    return render_template('404.html'), 404

@app.errorhandler(500)
def internal_error(error):
    db.session.rollback()
    return render_template('500.html'), 500

# Initialize database
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True)
```

question: You are a code expert. Please use your professional knowledge to generate accurate and professional responses. Be sure to ensure that the code you generate is executable. Implement a laboratory instrument management system where users can search for instruments through the frontend, view detailed parameters, and check current status (available, occupied, under maintenance). Administrators have the authority to add new instruments, update instrument information, and manage maintenance records.

checklist.title: Is a complete instrument search system implemented?
checklist.description: Review whether the code implements comprehensive search functionality with multiple filters (e.g., by type, availability, location), auto-complete suggestions, and relevance sorting. Score 0 if no search is implemented, 5 if only basic keyword search exists, and 10 if advanced search with filters and sorting is fully implemented with proper indexing for performance.

checklist.title: Is the instrument detail view system properly implemented?
checklist.description: Check whether detailed instrument information displays are implemented, including technical specifications, images, documentation links, usage history, and current status indicators. The parameters should be organized in collapsible sections with proper data validation. Score 0 if missing, 5 if basic information display only, and 10 if comprehensive with interactive elements and proper data formatting.

checklist.title: Is the instrument status management system complete?
checklist.description: Evaluate whether the system properly tracks and displays instrument status (available, occupied, under maintenance), includes status change timestamps, responsible personnel information, and estimated availability times. The status change mechanism should include appropriate validation and notification workflows. Deduct 5 points if history tracking is missing, and 3 points if status updates lack audit trails.

checklist.title: Is the administrator management interface fully functional?
checklist.description: Assess whether the admin panel includes all required functionality: adding new instruments, updating information, managing maintenance records, and generating reports. Check for proper form validation, image uploads, and audit logging of all administrative actions. Deduct 5 points if batch operations are missing, and 3 points if the interface lacks confirmation dialogs for critical operations.

checklist.title: Is the code robust?
checklist.description: Evaluate whether the code can handle common abnormal situations (such as network failures, invalid inputs, concurrent edits, etc.) and provide friendly error prompts or recovery mechanisms. Code with strong robustness should have proper exception handling, input validation, and data consistency checks. Give 10 points for comprehensive error handling, 5 points for basic validation, and 0 points if exceptions are unhandled.

checklist.title: Are there any innovative features that are eye-catching?
checklist.description: Check whether the code includes surprise features that enhance the experience (e.g., 1. Real-time equipment status visualization with floor maps 2. QR code generation for physical instrument tagging 3. Maintenance prediction algorithms based on usage patterns). Add 3 points for each practical innovative feature implemented (maximum 10 points).

checklist.title: Are there any redundant features?
checklist.description: Strictly check three types of redundancy: 1. Redundant implementation of similar functions (e.g., multiple ways to edit the same information) 2. Function modules unrelated to instrument management (e.g., built-in chat that could be handled by external systems) 3. Fancy effects that affect performance (e.g., unnecessary animations that slow page loading). Deduct 3 points for each redundancy found, and directly deduct 10 points if the core functions are interfered with by redundant code.

checklist.title: Does the code have engineering quality?
checklist.description: Review modular design (such as separating data access/business logic/presentation layers), unit test coverage, and build process automation. Deduct 5 points if global state pollution is found or design patterns are not used; deduct 5 points if the code duplication rate is too high (over 30%); deduct 5 points if the build process is not automated. The full score is 10 points.

checklist.title: Does the interface vision meet professional design standards?
checklist.description: Evaluate whether the overall design follows modern design principles: 1) Harmonious color matching (no more than 3 primary colors) 2) Proper layout spacing (element spacing follows the 8px multiple principle) 3) Professional font system (body font size ≥ 14px, line height over 1.5 times). Deduct 3 points for each crowded visual element, 5 points for a glaring color combination, and 5 points for chaotic text-image layout. The full score is 10 points.

checklist.title: Is the dynamic interaction smooth and seamless?
checklist.description: Judge whether the dynamic effects conform to human perception characteristics: 1) Click feedback delay ≤ 100ms 2) Transition animation duration controlled between 300-500ms 3) Clear visual focus guidance. Deduct 5 points for each operation without feedback, 3 points for visual after-images during fast sliding, and 5 points for hard-to-find key function buttons. The full score is 10 points.

```python
import cv2
import numpy as np
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, messagebox
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
import os

class ImageMattingTool:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = root
        self.root.title("Image Matting Tool")
        self.root.geometry("1000x700")
        
        # Initialize variables
        self.image = None
        self.original_image = None
        self.mask = None
        self.is_drawing = False
        self.brush_size = 5
        self.brush_color = (255, 255, 255)  # White for selection
        self.current_color = (255, 255, 255)
        self.canvas = None
        self.photo = None
        self.canvas_image = None
        
        # Create UI elements
        self.create_widgets()
        
    def create_widgets(self):
        # Create menu bar
        menubar = tk.Menu(self.root)
        file_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Open Image", command=self.open_image)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Save Result", command=self.save_result)
        file_menu.add_separator()
        file_menu.add_command(label="Exit", command=self.root.quit)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="File", menu=file_menu)
        
        self.root.config(menu=menubar)
        
        # Create canvas for image display
        self.canvas_frame = tk.Frame(self.root)
        self.canvas_frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True, padx=10, pady=10)
        
        # Create canvas for image display
        self.canvas = tk.Canvas(self.canvas_frame, bg='white')
        self.canvas.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        # Create control panel
        control_frame = tk.Frame(self.root)
        control_frame.pack(fill=tk.X, padx=10, pady=5)
        
        # Brush size slider
        tk.Label(control_frame, text="Brush Size:").pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        self.brush_slider = tk.Scale(control_frame, from_=1, to=50, orient=tk.HORIZONTAL, command=self.update_brush_size)
        self.brush_slider.set(self.brush_size)
        self.brush_slider.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        
        # Color selection
        tk.Label(control_frame, text="Color:").pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        self.color_var = tk.StringVar(value="White")
        color_options = ["White", "Black", "Red", "Green", "Blue"]
        color_menu = tk.OptionMenu(control_frame, self.color_var, *color_options, command=self.update_color)
        color_menu.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        
        # Buttons
        button_frame = tk.Frame(control_frame)
        button_frame.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=10)
        
        tk.Button(button_frame, text="Select", command=self.start_drawing).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        tk.Button(button_frame, text="Deselect", command=self.stop_drawing).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        tk.Button(button_frame, text="Reset", command=self.reset_mask).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        
        # Bind mouse events
        self.canvas.bind("<Button-1>", self.on_mouse_down)
        self.canvas.bind("<B1-Motion>", self.on_mouse_drag)
        self.canvas.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", self.on_mouse_up)
        
        # Initialize canvas
        self.canvas.bind("<Configure>", self.on_canvas_resize)
        
    def open_image(self):
        """Open an image file"""
        file_path = filedialog.askopenfilename(
            title="Select Image",
            filetypes=[("Image files", "*.jpg *.jpeg *.png *.bmp *.tiff")]
        )
        if not file_path:
            return
        
        self.image = cv2.imread(file_path)
        if self.image is None:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Could not load image")
            return
        
        self.original_image = self.image.copy()
        self.mask = np.zeros_like(self.image[:, :, 0])  # Initialize mask
        
        # Convert to RGB for PIL
        self.display_image(self.image)
        
    def display_image(self, image):
        """Display image on canvas"""
        if image is None:
            return
            
        # Convert BGR to RGB
        image_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        pil_image = Image.fromarray(image_rgb)
        self.photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image=pil_image)
        
        # Update canvas
        self.canvas.delete("all")
        self.canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor=tk.NW, image=self.photo)
        self.canvas_image = self.photo
        
        # Update canvas size
        self.canvas.config(width=self.photo.width(), height=self.photo.height())
        
    def update_brush_size(self, value):
        """Update brush size"""
        self.brush_size = int(value)
        
    def update_color(self, color):
        """Update brush color"""
        if color == "White":
            self.current_color = (255, 255, 255)
        elif color == "Black":
            self.current_color = (0, 0, 0)
        elif color == "Red":
            self.current_color = (255, 0, 0)
        elif color == "Green":
            self.current_color = (0, 255, 0)
        elif color == "Blue":
            self.current_color = (0, 0, 255)
            
    def start_drawing(self):
        """Start drawing mode"""
        self.is_drawing = True
        
    def stop_drawing(self):
        """Stop drawing mode"""
        self.is_drawing = False
        
    def reset_mask(self):
        """Reset mask to all zeros"""
        if self.mask is not None:
            self.mask = np.zeros_like(self.image[:, :, 0])
        self.update_display()
        
    def on_canvas_resize(self, event):
        """Handle canvas resize"""
        if self.photo:
            self.canvas.config(width=self.photo.width(), height=self.photo.height())
            
    def on_mouse_down(self, event):
        """Handle mouse down event"""
        if not self.is_drawing:
            return
            
        x, y = event.x, event.y
        
        # Convert canvas coordinates to image coordinates
        if self.image is not None:
            # Get image dimensions
            img_width, img_height = self.image.shape[1], self.image.shape[0]
            
            # Calculate scale factors
            canvas_width = self.canvas.winfo_width()
            canvas_height = self.canvas.winfo_height()
            
            # Calculate scale
            scale_x = canvas_width / img_width
            scale_y = canvas_height / img_height
            
            # Convert canvas coordinates to image coordinates
            img_x = int(x / scale_x)
            img_y = int(y / scale_y)
            
            # Ensure coordinates are within bounds
            img_x = max(0, min(img_x, img_width - 1))
            img_y = max(0, min(img_y, img_height - 1))
            
            # Draw on mask
            self.draw_on_mask(img_x, img_y)
            
    def on_mouse_drag(self, event):
        """Handle mouse drag event"""
        if not self.is_drawing:
            return
            
        x, y = event.x, event.y
        
        # Convert canvas coordinates to image coordinates
        if self.image is not None:
            # Get image dimensions
            img_width, img_height = self.image.shape[1], self.image.shape[0]
            
            # Calculate scale factors
            canvas_width = self.canvas.winfo_width()
            canvas_height = self.canvas.winfo_height()
            
            # Calculate scale
            scale_x = canvas_width / img_width
            scale_y = canvas_height / img_height
            
            # Convert canvas coordinates to image coordinates
            img_x = int(x / scale_x)
            img_y = int(y / scale_y)
            
            # Ensure coordinates are within bounds
            img_x = max(0, min(img_x, img_width - 1))
            img_y = max(0, min(img_y, img_height - 1))
            
            # Draw on mask
            self.draw_on_mask(img_x, img_y)
            
    def on_mouse_up(self, event):
        """Handle mouse up event"""
        pass
        
    def draw_on_mask(self, x, y):
        """Draw on mask"""
        if self.mask is not None:
            # Create a kernel for drawing
            kernel = np.ones((self.brush_size * 2 + 1, self.brush_size * 2 + 1), np.uint8)
            
            # Create a mask for the brush
            brush_mask = np.zeros_like(self.mask)
            brush_mask[x - self.brush_size:x + self.brush_size + 1, y - self.brush_size:y + self.brush_size + 1] = 255
            
            # Apply the brush to the mask
            self.mask = cv2.dilate(brush_mask, kernel, iterations=1)
            
            # Update display
            self.update_display()
            
    def update_display(self):
        """Update display with current mask"""
        if self.image is None or self.mask is None:
            return
            
        # Create result image
        result = self.image.copy()
        # Apply mask
        result[:, :, 0] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 0], self.mask)
        result[:, :, 1] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 1], self.mask)
        result[:, :, 2] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 2], self.mask)
        
        # Convert to RGB for PIL
        result_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(result, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        pil_image = Image.fromarray(result_rgb)
        self.photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image=pil_image)
        
        # Update canvas
        self.canvas.delete("all")
        self.canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor=tk.NW, image=self.photo)
        self.canvas_image = self.photo
        
        # Update canvas size
        self.canvas.config(width=self.photo.width(), height=self.photo.height())
        
    def save_result(self):
        """Save result image with transparent background"""
        if self.image is None:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "No image loaded")
            return
            
        # Create result image with transparent background
        result = self.image.copy()
        
        # Apply mask
        result[:, :, 0] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 0], self.mask)
        result[:, :, 1] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 1], self.mask)
        result[:, :, 2] = cv2.bitwise_and(result[:, :, 2], self.mask)
        
        # Create alpha channel
        alpha = np.zeros_like(self.mask)
        alpha[self.mask > 0] = 255
        
        # Combine image and alpha channel
        result_with_alpha = np.dstack((result, alpha))
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        pil_image = Image.fromarray(result_with_alpha)
        
        # Save image
        file_path = filedialog.asksaveasfilename(
            title="Save Result",
            defaultextension=".png",
            filetypes=[("PNG files", "*.png"), ("All files", "*.*")]
        )
        if file_path:
            pil_image.save(file_path, format="PNG")
            messagebox.showinfo("Success", "Image saved successfully")
            
if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = tk.Tk()
    app = ImageMattingTool(root)
    root.mainloop()
```

This code creates a complete image matting tool with the following features:

1. Users can open an image file
2. Users can brush over areas they want to keep (white areas in the mask)
3. Areas not selected will be made transparent
4. Users can adjust brush size and color
5. Users can save the result with a transparent background

The tool uses a simple masking approach where:
- White areas in the mask = areas to keep
- Black areas in the mask = areas to make transparent

The interface includes:
- Canvas for displaying the image
- Control panel with brush size slider, color selection, and buttons
- Menu for opening and saving images

The tool is designed to be simple and intuitive for users to select areas they want to keep in an image.

Below is a comprehensive implementation of a learning partner matching system that intelligently pairs users based on learning goals, interests, and time schedules. The system includes user management, matching algorithm, invitation system, and feedback mechanism for continuous optimization.

```python
import uuid
import datetime
import random
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from collections import defaultdict

class LearningGoal(Enum):
    """Enum for different learning goals"""
    TECHNICAL_SKILLS = "Technical Skills"
    LANGUAGE_LEARNING = "Language Learning"
    ACADEMIC_COURSES = "Academic Courses"
    CERTIFICATIONS = "Certifications"
    HOBBY_DEVELOPMENT = "Hobby Development"
    PROFESSIONAL_DEVELOPMENT = "Professional Development"
    OTHER = "Other"

class InterestCategory(Enum):
    """Enum for different interest categories"""
    TECHNOLOGY = "Technology"
    ARTS = "Arts"
    SCIENCE = "Science"
    BUSINESS = "Business"
    HEALTH = "Health"
    EDUCATION = "Education"
    OTHER = "Other"

class TimePreference(Enum):
    """Enum for time preferences"""
    MORNING = "Morning (6-12 AM)"
    AFTERNOON = "Afternoon (12-6 PM)"
    EVENING = "Evening (6-12 AM)"
    NIGHT = "Night (12 AM-6 AM)"
    FLEXIBLE = "Flexible"

@dataclass
class User:
    """User data class"""
    user_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str
    email: str
    learning_goals: List[LearningGoal] = field(default_factory=list)
    interests: List[InterestCategory] = field(default_factory=list)
    time_preferences: List[TimePreference] = field(default_factory=list)
    availability: Dict[str, List[datetime.time]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    bio: str = ""
    location: str = ""
    experience_level: str = "Beginner"
    created_at: datetime.datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)
    last_active: datetime.datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        # Initialize availability if not provided
        if not self.availability:
            self.availability = {
                "weekdays": [],
                "weekends": []
            }

@dataclass
class Match:
    """Match data class"""
    match_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    user1_id: str
    user2_id: str
    match_score: float = 0.0
    created_at: datetime.datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)
    status: str = "pending"  # pending, accepted, rejected, expired
    invitation_sent: bool = False
    invitation_time: Optional[datetime.datetime] = None

@dataclass
class Invitation:
    """Invitation data class"""
    invitation_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    from_user_id: str
    to_user_id: str
    message: str = "I'd love to collaborate with you on our learning goals!"
    sent_at: datetime.datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)
    accepted: bool = False
    accepted_at: Optional[datetime.datetime] = None
    rejected: bool = False
    rejected_at: Optional[datetime.datetime] = None

@dataclass
class Feedback:
    """Feedback data class for matching algorithm optimization"""
    feedback_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    match_id: str
    user_id: str
    rating: int = 5  # 1-5 scale
    comment: str = ""
    submitted_at: datetime.datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.datetime.now)

class LearningPartnerMatcher:
    """Main class for learning partner matching system"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.users: Dict[str, User] = {}
        self.matches: Dict[str, Match] = {}
        self.invitations: Dict[str, Invitation] = {}
        self.feedback: Dict[str, Feedback] = {}
        self.match_history: Dict[str, List[Match]] = defaultdict(list)
        self.user_preferences: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        
    def add_user(self, user: User) -> str:
        """Add a new user to the system"""
        self.users[user.user_id] = user
        return user.user_id
    
    def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get a user by ID"""
        return self.users.get(user_id)
    
    def update_user(self, user_id: str, **kwargs) -> bool:
        """Update user information"""
        if user_id not in self.users:
            return False
        
        user = self.users[user_id]
        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            if hasattr(user, key):
                setattr(user, key, value)
        return True
    
    def get_all_users(self) -> List[User]:
        """Get all users"""
        return list(self.users.values())
    
    def calculate_match_score(self, user1: User, user2: User) -> float:
        """Calculate match score based on learning goals, interests, and time preferences"""
        score = 0.0
        
        # Goal similarity (weight: 30%)
        goal_similarity = self._calculate_goal_similarity(user1, user2)
        score += goal_similarity * 0.3
        
        # Interest similarity (weight: 30%)
        interest_similarity = self._calculate_interest_similarity(user1, user2)
        score += interest_similarity * 0.3
        
        # Time preference similarity (weight: 20%)
        time_similarity = self._calculate_time_similarity(user1, user2)
        score += time_similarity * 0.2
        
        # Availability overlap (weight: 20%)
        availability_similarity = self._calculate_availability_similarity(user1, user2)
        score += availability_similarity * 0.2
        
        return min(max(score, 0.0), 1.0)
    
    def _calculate_goal_similarity(self, user1: User, user2: User) -> float:
        """Calculate similarity based on learning goals"""
        common_goals = set(user1.learning_goals) & set(user2.learning_goals)
        total_goals = len(set(user1.learning_goals) | set(user2.learning_goals))
        
        if total_goals == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return len(common_goals) / total_goals
    
    def _calculate_interest_similarity(self, user1: User, user2: User) -> float:
        """Calculate similarity based on interests"""
        common_interests = set(user1.interests) & set(user2.interests)
        total_interests = len(set(user1.interests) | set(user2.interests))
        
        if total_interests == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return len(common_interests) / total_interests
    
    def _calculate_time_similarity(self, user1: User, user2: User) -> float:
        """Calculate similarity based on time preferences"""
        # Count overlapping time preferences
        common_preferences = set(user1.time_preferences) & set(user2.time_preferences)
        total_preferences = len(set(user1.time_preferences) | set(user2.time_preferences))
        
        if total_preferences == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return len(common_preferences) / total_preferences
    
    def _calculate_availability_similarity(self, user1: User, user2: User) -> float:
        """Calculate similarity based on availability"""
        # Simple availability check - if both have overlapping availability
        # In a real system, this would be more sophisticated with actual time slots
        weekdays1 = set(user1.availability.get("weekdays", []))
        weekdays2 = set(user2.availability.get("weekdays", []))
        weekends1 = set(user1.availability.get("weekends", []))
        weekends2 = set(user2.availability.get("weekends", []))
        
        # Check if any common availability exists
        weekday_overlap = len(weekdays1 & weekdays2)
        weekend_overlap = len(weekends1 & weekends2)
        
        total_overlap = weekday_overlap + weekend_overlap
        total_possible = len(weekdays1) + len(weekdays2) + len(weekends1) + len(weekends2)
        
        if total_possible == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return total_overlap / total_possible
    
    def find_matches(self, user_id: str, limit: int = 5) -> List[Match]:
        """Find potential matches for a user"""
        user = self.get_user(user_id)
        if not user:
            return []
        
        potential_matches = []
        
        for other_user_id, other_user in self.users.items():
            if other_user_id == user_id:
                continue
            
            # Calculate match score
            score = self.calculate_match_score(user, other_user)
            match = Match(
                match_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                user1_id=user_id,
                user2_id=other_user_id,
                match_score=score,
                created_at=datetime.datetime.now()
            )
            potential_matches.append(match)
        
        # Sort by score (descending) and return top matches
        potential_matches.sort(key=lambda x: x.match_score, reverse=True)
        return potential_matches[:limit]
    
    def send_invitation(self, from_user_id: str, to_user_id: str, message: str = "") -> str:
        """Send an invitation to a potential match"""
        if from_user_id not in self.users or to_user_id not in self.users:
            raise ValueError("User not found")
        
        invitation = Invitation(
            invitation_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            from_user_id=from_user_id,
            to_user_id=to_user_id,
            message=message
        )
        
        self.invitations[invitation.invitation_id] = invitation
        return invitation.invitation_id
    
    def accept_invitation(self, invitation_id: str) -> bool:
        """Accept an invitation"""
        if invitation_id not in self.invitations:
            return False
        
        invitation = self.invitations[invitation_id]
        invitation.accepted = True
        invitation.accepted_at = datetime.datetime.now()
        
        # Create a match record
        match = Match(
            match_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            user1_id=invitation.from_user_id,
            user2_id=invitation.to_user_id,
            match_score=invitation.match_score if hasattr(invitation, 'match_score') else 0.0,
            created_at=datetime.datetime.now(),
            status="accepted"
        )
        
        self.matches[match.match_id] = match
        self.match_history[invitation.from_user_id].append(match)
        self.match_history[invitation.to_user_id].append(match)
        
        return True
    
    def reject_invitation(self, invitation_id: str) -> bool:
        """Reject an invitation"""
        if invitation_id not in self.invitations:
            return False
        
        invitation = self.invitations[invitation_id]
        invitation.rejected = True
        invitation.rejected_at = datetime.datetime.now()
        
        return True
    
    def submit_feedback(self, match_id: str, user_id: str, rating: int, comment: str = "") -> str:
        """Submit feedback for a match"""
        if match_id not in self.matches:
            return False
        
        feedback = Feedback(
            feedback_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            match_id=match_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            rating=rating,
            comment=comment,
            submitted_at=datetime.datetime.now()
        )
        
        self.feedback[feedback.feedback_id] = feedback
        return feedback.feedback_id
    
    def get_match_history(self, user_id: str) -> List[Match]:
        """Get match history for a user"""
        return self.match_history.get(user_id, [])
    
    def get_invitations(self, user_id: str) -> List[Invitation]:
        """Get invitations for a user"""
        # Get all invitations where user is the recipient
        invitations = [inv for inv in self.invitations.values() if inv.to_user_id == user_id]
        return invitations
    
    def get_pending_matches(self, user_id: str) -> List[Match]:
        """Get pending matches for a user"""
        pending_matches = []
        for match in self.matches.values():
            if match.status == "pending" and (match.user1_id == user_id or match.user2_id == user_id):
                pending_matches.append(match)
        return pending_matches
    
    def get_user_matches(self, user_id: str) -> List[Match]:
        """Get all matches for a user"""
        matches = []
        for match in self.matches.values():
            if match.user1_id == user_id or match.user2_id == user_id:
                matches.append(match)
        return matches
    
    def get_match_statistics(self) -> Dict:
        """Get statistics about matches"""
        total_matches = len(self.matches)
        total_invitations = len(self.invitations)
        total_feedback = len(self.feedback)
        
        # Calculate average match score
        total_score = sum(match.match_score for match in self.matches.values())
        avg_score = total_score / total_matches if total_matches > 0 else 0
        
        # Calculate match acceptance rate
        accepted_matches = sum(1 for match in self.matches.values() if match.status == "accepted")
        acceptance_rate = accepted_matches / total_matches if total_matches > 0 else 0
        
        return {
            "total_matches": total_matches,
            "total_invitations": total_invitations,
            "total_feedback": total_feedback,
            "average_match_score": avg_score,
            "acceptance_rate": acceptance_rate
        }
    
    def optimize_algorithm(self):
        """Optimize matching algorithm based on feedback"""
        # Analyze feedback to improve matching algorithm
        # This is a simplified version - in practice, this would involve
        # machine learning or statistical analysis
        
        # Get all feedback
        feedbacks = list(self.feedback.values())
        
        if not feedbacks:

        match_ratings = defaultdict(list)

            match_ratings[feedback.match_id].append(feedback.rating)

    # Create sample users

        interests=[InterestCategory.TECHNOLOGY, InterestCategory.BUSINESS],
```

## System Features

This implementation includes:

1. **User Management**: Create, retrieve, and update user profiles with learning goals, interests, time preferences, and availability.

2. **Intelligent Matching Algorithm**: Calculate match scores based on:
   - Learning goals similarity (30% weight)
   - Interests similarity (30% weight)
   - Time preferences similarity (20% weight)
   - Availability overlap (20% weight)

3. **Invitation System**: Users can send invitations to potential matches with custom messages.

4. **Feedback Mechanism**: Users can rate matches (1-5 scale) and provide comments to help optimize the algorithm.

5. **Match History**: Track all matches, including status (pending, accepted, rejected).

6. **Statistics**: Get system-wide statistics including average match scores and acceptance rates.

7. **Optimization**: Simple algorithm to improve matching based on user feedback.

## Key Design Decisions

- **Scalable Architecture**: Uses UUIDs for unique identifiers and dictionaries for efficient lookups.
- **Extensible**: Easy to add new learning goals, interests, or time preferences.
- **Flexible**: Users can have multiple preferences in each category.
- **Realistic**: Includes availability tracking and time-based matching.

## Potential Enhancements

1. **Machine Learning Integration**: Use clustering or collaborative filtering for more sophisticated matching.
2. **Real-time Matching**: Implement WebSocket or polling for real-time match suggestions.
3. **Mobile Optimization**: Add mobile-friendly UI components.
4. **Gamification**: Add badges, streaks, or leaderboards for engagement.
5. **Advanced Availability**: Implement calendar integration for precise time slot matching.
6. **Language Support**: Add multilingual support for global users.

This system provides a solid foundation for a learning partner matching platform that can be extended and customized based on specific requirements.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

@dataclass
class CharacterInfoPanel:
    """Character Information Panel for a Novel Character"""
    
    name: str
    race: str
    age: int
    gender: str
    awakened_bloodline: str
    potential: str
    background: str
    personality: str
    abilities: list[str]
    current_status: str
    origin: str
    special_notes: str

    def display_panel(self):
        """Display the character information panel in a formatted way"""
        print("=" * 60)
        print(f"CHARACTER PROFILE: {self.name.upper()}")
        print("=" * 60)
        print(f"Race: {self.race}")
        print(f"Age: {self.age}")
        print(f"Gender: {self.gender}")
        print(f"Awakened Bloodline: {self.awakened_bloodline}")
        print(f"Potential: {self.potential}")
        print(f"Background: {self.background}")
        print(f"Personality: {self.personality}")
        print(f"Abilities: {', '.join(self.abilities) if self.abilities else 'None'}")
        print(f"Current Status: {self.current_status}")
        print(f"Origin: {self.origin}")
        print(f"Special Notes: {self.special_notes}")
        print("=" * 60)

# Example character: Human female who has awakened the Yan-Huang bloodline
yan_huang_female = CharacterInfoPanel(
    name="Li Xue",
    race="Human",
    age=22,
    gender="Female",
    awakened_bloodline="Yan-Huang Bloodline",
    potential="Legendary - Unparalleled Martial and Spiritual Potential",
    background="Born in the remote mountains of the Eastern Kingdom, raised by her grandmother who was a secret guardian of ancient bloodline knowledge.",
    personality="Calm, introspective, fiercely loyal, with a hidden streak of rebelliousness.",
    abilities=[
        "Bloodline Awakening: Access to primordial martial arts and divine energy",
        "Heavenly Essence Channeling: Manipulate cosmic energy for healing and combat",
        "Yan-Huang Seal: Can temporarily summon ancestral warriors to aid in battle",
        "Divine Sight: See through illusions and detect hidden threats"
    ],
    current_status="Active Warrior - Training under the guidance of the last Yan-Huang Guardian",
    origin="Eastern Kingdom - Mountains of the First Dawn",
    special_notes="Her bloodline is dormant until triggered by great danger or emotional trauma. She is the first human female to awaken this lineage in 3000 years."
)

# Display the character panel
yan_huang_female.display_panel()
```

This code defines a `CharacterInfoPanel` class that encapsulates all the necessary details for a novel character, including race, age, awakened bloodline, potential, and other attributes. It also includes a `display_panel()` method to format and display the information in a visually appealing way.

The example character, **Li Xue**, is a human female who has awakened the Yan-Huang bloodline — a rare and powerful lineage with ancient martial and spiritual capabilities. The panel includes her background, personality, abilities, current status, origin, and special notes to enrich the narrative context.
